Brightness is a Float property of PointLight that controls the emission intensity of the light. It affects how bright the light appears but does not influence its range. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4 scripting, this property cannot be assigned via code and initially reads as nil. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/point-light.md

Color is a Color3 property of PointLight that determines the color of the light being emitted. Darker color values produce a similar visual effect to turning the light off. In runtime scripting, it accepts and retains a Color3 value, even though the instance itself is otherwise non-functional. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/point-light.md

Range is a Float property of PointLight that defines the maximum spherical distance the light can reach. It controls how the brightness falls off with distance but does not increase the light's overall brightness. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, it is not settable from scripts. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/point-light.md

Name is a String property inherited from Instance that sets the label of the PointLight as it is shown in the hierarchy explorer. It functions the same way as the Name property on other Vortex instances. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/point-light.md

questions: What is PointLight runtime scripting limitation?
Explain PointLight runtime scripting limitation in Vortex
How do I use PointLight runtime scripting limitation?
Tell me about PointLight runtime scripting limitation
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calling Instance.new("PointLight") from a Script or LocalScript creates a non-functional shell rather than a working light. Generic Instance methods and a Changed signal are exposed, but Brightness, Range, Enabled, and Shadows read as nil and cannot be set. While Color retains an assigned Color3, setting Parent on the shell does not actually attach it to a Part, so there is no working scripted way to configure or render a PointLight at runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/point-light.md

RemoteEvent is a class used for sending information between the server and clients in Vortex. It supports both server-to-client and client-to-server communication, and is typically parented under ReplicatedStorage so both sides can access it via WaitForChild. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

FireAllClients is a RemoteEvent method that fires data to every connected client. Its signature is FireAllClients(arguments: Tuple) and it returns nothing; the data is delivered to each client's OnClientEvent handler. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

FireClient is a RemoteEvent method used by the server to send data to one specific client. Its signature is FireClient(player: Player, arguments: Tuple) and returns nothing. Note that in Vortex 0.3.4, the method is exposed but its delivery has not yet been confirmed. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

FireServer is a RemoteEvent method called from the client to send data to the server. Its signature is FireServer(arguments: Tuple) and returns nothing. It triggers the server-side OnServerEvent handler and was confirmed working in Vortex Studio 0.3.4 for editor-authored remotes in ReplicatedStorage. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

OnClientEvent is a RemoteEvent signal fired on the client when the server sends data via FireClient or FireAllClients. Its signature is OnClientEvent(arguments: Tuple): Signal. The event is exposed in Vortex 0.3.4, although delivery has not yet been fully established. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

OnServerEvent is a RemoteEvent signal fired on the server when a client invokes FireServer. Its signature is OnServerEvent(senderId: Number, arguments: Tuple): Signal. In Vortex the senderId is a numeric connection identifier rather than a Player object, so it cannot currently be mapped back to a specific player, character, or humanoid. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

RemoteFunction is a networking object in Vortex that, unlike RemoteEvent, lets data be computed inside a function call and the resulting values returned to the caller. It supports calling from server to client and from client to server, but does not support an InvokeAllClients because reliably yielding until every player has returned a value is not guaranteed. Instances of RemoteFunction are typically parented under ReplicatedStorage so both server and client scripts can access them. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

InvokeClient is a method on RemoteFunction used by the server to invoke data from the server to a specific client. Its signature is InvokeClient(player: Player, arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where player is the target Player and arguments is a tuple of values sent to the client, and it yields until the client returns a tuple response via OnClientInvoke. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

InvokeServer is a method on RemoteFunction used by the client to invoke data from the client to the server. Its signature is InvokeServer(arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where arguments is a tuple of values sent to the server, and it returns the tuple that the server produces via its OnServerInvoke callback. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

OnClientInvoke is a writable callback on RemoteFunction that runs on the client in response to InvokeClient from the server. Its signature is OnClientInvoke(arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where arguments is the tuple the server passed, and whatever tuple it returns is sent back to the server. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

OnServerInvoke is a writable callback on RemoteFunction that runs on the server in response to InvokeServer from a client. Its signature is OnServerInvoke(senderId: Number, arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where senderId is a numeric identifier for the invoking client and arguments is the tuple the client sent; the returned tuple is delivered back to that client. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

questions: What are the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations?
Explain the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations
How do I handle the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations?
Tell me about the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, InvokeServer is exposed on the client and OnServerInvoke can be assigned in a Script for an editor-authored RemoteFunction under ReplicatedStorage. However, InvokeServer(LocalPlayer) is rejected before delivery because Instances cannot currently be sent through remotes, so a successful primitive request/response round trip has not yet been established. The server-side Players:GetChildren() route is unavailable, but Players:GetPlayers() does return visible Player objects in a server Script, providing the Player target in principle. OnClientInvoke and InvokeClient delivery are still untested in this version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

ReplicatedStorage is a service container whose contents are loaded by both the server and the client. Instances placed inside it automatically have their properties synced from the server to clients. It is accessed via game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

ClassName is a String property of ReplicatedStorage that holds the runtime class name of the service. It is read-only and identifies the service type during execution. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

Name is a String property of ReplicatedStorage that stores the service name shown by the runtime. It identifies the service within the game's hierarchy. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

FindFirstChild is a method on ReplicatedStorage with the signature ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(name: String). It returns the first direct child matching the supplied name, or nil if no such child exists. Only direct (non-recursive) children are searched. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

GetChildren is a method on ReplicatedStorage that returns an array of Instance values representing the direct children of the service. It provides a snapshot of the immediate contents rather than a recursive listing. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

WaitForChild is a method on ReplicatedStorage with the signature ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild(name: String). It blocks until a direct child with the supplied name appears and then returns that Instance. It is useful for synchronizing code that depends on a replicated instance that may not exist yet at runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

questions: What is Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage?
Explain Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage in Vortex
How do I use Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage?
Tell me about Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage
answer: To place an instance into ReplicatedStorage, the developer creates it with Instance.new and sets its Parent property to the ReplicatedStorage service. For example, a new Part can be named "SharedPart" and assigned as a child of ReplicatedStorage so that both server and client can see it. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

questions: What is Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes?
Explain Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes in Vortex
How do I use Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes?
Tell me about Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes
answer: These notes document observed behavior in Vortex Studio version 0.3.4 and may not apply to later releases. They confirm that a temporary Part can be parented to ReplicatedStorage and that WaitForChild will resolve it, while FindFirstChild returns nil and GetChildren omits it under the same conditions. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

ServerScriptService is a Roblox-style service obtained via game:GetService("ServerScriptService") in Vortex Studio 0.3.4. It is accessible from both Script and LocalScript execution contexts and provides standard enumeration methods such as FindFirstChild, GetChildren, and WaitForChild. A notable limitation is that Scripts created at runtime do not appear as observable children of this service: parent-equality checks and FindFirstChild will not locate them, and GetChildren() will exclude them. To work reliably, server Scripts should be authored and placed in the editor rather than instantiated programmatically. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/server-script-service.md

SpawnLocation is a specialized Part used to define where player characters load into the world. It inherits from the base part class. Its primary purpose is providing a spawn point for players when they join or respawn. SpawnLocation inherits all standard Part properties such as Color, Transparency, Material, Cast Shadow, Anchored, CanCollide, Truss, Name, Position, Rotation, and Size. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spawnlocation.md

questions: Explain SpawnLocation runtime availability in Vortex
How do I use SpawnLocation runtime availability?
Tell me about SpawnLocation runtime availability
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calling Instance.new("SpawnLocation") fails in both Script and LocalScript contexts. A workspace descendant scan also did not find any live SpawnLocation instances in the tested project. This means the editor-facing property documentation is not confirmed to be a working runtime scripting surface in this version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spawnlocation.md

A SpotLight in Vortex is a conical light that emits from a single point in 3D space. It must be parented to a Part, and it inherits its position from the parent Part. There is no built-in on/off switch, but setting the Color, Brightness, Angle, or Range to 0 will visually disable the light. Under the Properties tab, SpotLight displays Position, Rotation, and Size attributes, but Position and Rotation are read-only while Size has no effect. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

questions: What is the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation?
Explain the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation in Vortex
How do I use the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation?
Tell me about the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calling Instance.new("SpotLight") succeeds in both Script and LocalScript but returns a non-functional shell. The instance only exposes generic Instance methods plus a connectable Changed signal, while the tested light-specific fields initially read as nil. Brightness, Range, Angle, Enabled, and Shadows cannot be set, and although Color accepts and retains a Color3 value, assigning Parent to a temporary Part does not actually establish parentage. As a result, there is no confirmed script route for configuring or attaching a rendered SpotLight in the current runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Angle is a Float property of a SpotLight that defines the spread of the emission cone. Smaller values produce a sharper, more focused cutoff, while wider values create a softer fall-off at the edges of the cone. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Brightness is a Float property of a SpotLight that controls how intensely the light is emitted. It affects only the strength of the light and does not influence how far the light reaches. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Color is a Color3 property of a SpotLight that determines the color tint of the emitted light. Darker colors effectively behave like turning the light off. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Face is an Enum.Face property of a SpotLight that selects which face of the parent Part the light is emitted from. By choosing a different face, the direction of the cone can be aimed along a specific axis of the parent. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Name is a String property of a SpotLight that serves as both the internal identifier and the label shown in the Explorer panel. Changing it renames the instance in the hierarchy. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Range is a Float property of a SpotLight that specifies the maximum linear distance the light can reach. It governs how the brightness falls off over distance, but increasing it does not make the light itself brighter. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

StarterPlayerScripts is a container located inside the StarterPlayer service that holds client-side scripts. When a player joins the experience, the contents of StarterPlayerScripts are automatically copied into that player's PlayerScripts container. It is designed primarily for LocalScripts, which execute on the client side of the experience. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

PlayerScripts is the per-player destination container where scripts from StarterPlayerScripts are copied when a player joins the experience. It serves as the runtime location for client-side scripts associated with that specific player during their session. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

StarterPlayerScripts is commonly used for client-side game systems, player input handling, camera systems, client-side effects and animations, user interface logic, keyboard, mouse, and controller input, local player movement systems, and client-side visual effects. It houses code that runs on the player's device for player-specific behavior. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

questions: Explain the StarterCharacterScripts distinction in Vortex
How do I use the StarterCharacterScripts distinction?
Tell me about the StarterCharacterScripts distinction
answer: StarterCharacterScripts should not be confused with StarterPlayerScripts. Although both look similar, they have different purposes: StarterPlayerScripts focuses on client-side player systems, while StarterCharacterScripts is intended for scripts tied to the player's character specifically. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

questions: What script types run in StarterPlayerScripts?
Explain script types in StarterPlayerScripts in Vortex
How do I use script types in StarterPlayerScripts?
Tell me about script types in StarterPlayerScripts
answer: StarterPlayerScripts is primarily intended for LocalScripts, which run on the client. Server Scripts placed there will not run on the server. ModuleScripts can be placed inside StarterPlayerScripts when they will be required by other client-side scripts, but for modules that need to be shared by both client and server, ReplicatedStorage is the recommended location. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

questions: What are the StarterPlayerScripts security considerations?
How do I use StarterPlayerScripts security considerations?
answer: StarterPlayerScripts should never be used for server-side security or validation, since the client is controlled by the player and cannot be trusted. Server validation, anti-cheat enforcement, and other security-critical logic must always run on the server rather than in client-side scripts placed in StarterPlayerScripts. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md
